title: Commitment Currency: translating VIP asks into sprintable roadmap allocations
creator: Mariana Rivera
description: Define and pilot a deterministic framework that converts top-customer requests (VIP asks) into a standardized unit we call Commitment Currency (CCU). CCUs make fiscal and scheduling trade-offs explicit by mapping customer impact, technical complexity, and cross-org dependencies to sprintable allocations. The framework will be used by PMs to adjudicate admission, by Eng to estimate deliverability, and by Sales/CS to set customer expectations and SLAs.
background: We currently handle VIP feature requests via ad-hoc lanes: some get expedited, others sit in backlog. This creates inconsistent commitments, hidden delivery debt, and unclear expectations for top accounts. Leadership wants a repeatable mechanism that: 1) quantifies the value/effort trade-off, 2) guarantees a bounded response window, and 3) provides an audit trail for commitment decisions (for renewals and escalations).
goals: Operationalize a 3-factor scoring model (Impact x Urgency x Complexity) into a single CCU value
Create a transparent ledger that maps CCUs to sprint capacity and commitment windows
Reduce time-to-decision for VIP asks to under 7 business days
Provide CS/Sales with deterministic expectation statements tied to CCU grants
success_metrics: % of VIP asks processed with CCU within 7 business days >= 90%
Variance between CCU-predicted and actual sprint effort <= 25% after 2 sprints
Customer satisfaction (follow-up survey) for VIP request handling >= 4.2/5
Number of escalations due to unclear commitments reduced by 60% in pilot accounts
proposed_flow: 1) Intake: CS files request with impact evidence; 2) Triage: PM applies scoring rubric and suggests CCU; 3) Engineering estimation converts CCU to planned sprint tickets (or escrowed CCUs if blocked); 4) Commitment: PM publishes a timeboxed commitment statement to customer; 5) Execution: Delivery tracked against CCU ledger; 6) Settlement: CCUs consumed or refunded depending on scope shifts.
scoring_components: Impact: revenue at risk / revenue upside / strategic alignment (weighted)
Urgency: contractual SLA, regulatory deadline, competitive risk
Complexity: cross-team work, infra changes, third-party dependencies
Confidence multiplier: historical on-time delivery for similar asks
acceptance_criteria: A defined CCU scoring sheet (spreadsheet + template) that PMs can use in the console intake form
Automation prototype: intake form returns a preliminary CCU and an explanation note
Pilot run with 3 enterprise customers where at least 5 VIP asks are processed through CCU and outcomes logged
Dashboard showing CCU ledger with committed CCUs, consumed CCUs, open escrows, and variance to actuals
milestones: Design rubric & scoring sheet — complete by 2025-02-05
Console intake integration (UI mock + backend hook) — ready for pilot by 2025-02-20
Engineering estimation conversion rules (CCU->story points mapping) — v0 by 2025-02-28
Pilot with 3 accounts and iterate — Feb 28 to Mar 14
Decision on org-wide rollout or refine — review meeting 2025-03-18
dependencies: Tracking telemetry endpoints for CCU ledger (infra-telemetry-3)
Support from Research for historical delivery variance data
Agreement from Sales/CS to run pilot with selected accounts
risks: Overfitting CCU weights to initial pilot accounts causing unfair prioritization
Engineering may under-index non-development effort (docs, rollout), skewing CCU accuracy
Customers may see CCU as a contractual promise if language is not carefully curated
Operational overhead: maintaining CCU ledger requires tooling investment
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal dry-run with PM/Eng for 10 mock asks (Feb 6-12)
Phase 1: Small pilot with 3 enterprise customers (Feb 20 - Mar 14)
Phase 2: Recalibrate CCU weights based on pilot variance (Mar 15-21)
Phase 3: Documentation, CS training, and provider SLA language updates (Mar 22 - Apr 5)
Phase 4: Gradual rollout to all high-touch accounts and measurement windows (Apr+)
